source.title: Infralimbic parvalbumin neural activity facilitates cued threat avoidance

confidence_rationale: High mapping fidelity on the anatomical/functional gate claim (this is IL specifically, not a PFC subregion analog, with a clean causal manipulation and a directly comparable freeze-suppression readout) -- but the paper's central learning-trajectory finding directly contradicts the piece of MECH-357 that carries its falsifiability (suppression must scale with LEARNED efficacy, not an early, non-scaling signal). Confidence reflects strong evidence on a genuinely mixed verdict, not weak evidence.
failure_signatures: IL PV movement-related activity during avoidance emerged tens of trials before animals had learned the avoidance response, immediately after a single shock exposure.

IL PV activity during the avoidance movement was not attenuated (or otherwise changed) by further learning (p=0.8886, one-way ANOVA) -- i.e. it did not scale with an accruing avoidance-efficacy signal.

Optogenetic suppression of IL PV neurons delayed avoidance latency and increased freezing duration during the tone -- freeze suppression is genuinely causal, not merely correlational, going the other direction from the failure signature above.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In PV-Cre mice performing two-way signaled active avoidance, infralimbic (IL) parvalbumin interneuron activity rises specifically during the avoidance movement (not reward approach or open-field locomotion; p=0.0077 vs. baseline). Optogenetic silencing of these neurons causally delays avoidance latency (p=0.0281) and increases freezing duration during the tone (p=0.0175), with movement toward reward and general locomotion unaffected -- i.e. a genuine, behaviorally-specific freeze-suppression gate that releases the avoidance action. This movement-locked IL-PV signal appears within tens of trials of the first shock, well before the avoidance response is learned, and its magnitude does not change with further training (p=0.8886).
mapping.ree_translation: The causal circuit-level claim -- IL activity gates a switch from freeze to instrumental avoidance -- is about as direct a biological analogue of MECH-357's pieces (a)+(b) (action-bias release + freeze-suppression override) as this literature offers: same region label (IL, not PL or generic vmPFC), same behavioral readout (freeze duration vs. avoidance latency), same causal design (bidirectional: record + suppress). But the learning-trajectory result cuts directly against MECH-357's OWN stated falsifiability condition: the claim explicitly requires suppression onset to track a LEARNED avoidance_efficacy eligibility trace rather than an instantaneous/early-emerging signal, precisely to keep MECH-357 distinct from the reflexive overrides SD-037/MECH-281. This paper's IL-PV gate is present from very early trials and is flat across learning -- structurally closer to the reflexive-override family MECH-357 is defined AGAINST than to the gradually-learned gate MECH-357 proposes. It does not falsify the existence of an IL-analog freeze-suppression gate; it weakens the specific claim that such a gate's strength is set by a learned efficacy trace rather than a threat-triggered, largely pre-wired switch.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Species is mouse, task is two-way signaled shuttle avoidance (footshock, tone CS) -- a different task structure from REE's foraging-under-hazard survival leg, and 'learning' here is measured behaviorally (avoidance acquisition curve) rather than as an internal scalar efficacy variable, so 'did not scale with learning' is an absence-of-effect claim about a specific cell population's calcium/optogenetic signature, not a direct disproof that some OTHER learned signal (e.g. a slower synaptic or circuit-level plasticity process feeding into that same gate) exists in this animal. The authors themselves note PV neurons likely 'shape rather than suppress' cortical activity via synchronization, a more complex mechanism than a simple binary gate, and that other interneuron classes (SOM, VIP) were not examined and could carry a learning-dependent contribution the PV population does not.
mapping.source_context: Male PV-Cre mice, 6-10 weeks to 10 months old; two-way signaled active avoidance (5 s tone-to-shock window, 0.3 mA, 2 s max shock), fiber photometry (GCaMP6f, n=8) and optogenetic inhibition (eNpHR, n=8 vs. n=5 eYFP controls) targeting IL PV interneurons.

confidence_components.notes: Weighted mapping_fidelity heavily given this is a mechanistic/architectural claim and the paper is unusually well-matched on region (IL) and behavioral readout (freeze-vs-avoidance) -- but transfer_risk is elevated because the SPECIFIC falsifiable element MECH-357 stakes its distinctness on (learned vs. reflexive suppression) is exactly what this paper's central result bears on, in the weakening direction, and only one interneuron population out of several plausible IL circuits was probed.
